final_answer: Two self-improvement directions are chosen — one quality lever and one speed lever — both hardened entirely by reusing existing mechanisms, with NO new layers. (1) QUALITY: 'Fail loud + signal hygiene' (atom A1, judge 0.89). This is the highest-leverage, data-grounded direction: restart-root-cause-log and audit.launches.jsonl show the dominant failure mode is silent/incomplete work that is never surfaced. Folded INTO this direction as facets (not separate directions): error-contract enforcement at the commit boundary (A4, accepted as a distinct lever but kept inside fail-loud to honor the 1–2-direction limit), the self-maintenance completion contract (A9 wins over A3: it is a SUBCASE of fail-loud, realized by A10/A11, not a standalone primary direction), and finding-dedup signal hygiene (A15). (2) SPEED: 'Depth-aware decomposition & routing' (A2 collapsed onto its concrete mechanism A14): integrate the EXISTING depth-router's depth-assessment into the task-ingestion gate so Standard plan-only tasks take a lighter pipeline weight, justified by planner_ms/verify_ms dominance in the metrics. Every hardening step is additive and confined to existing mechanisms — error contracts, audit ledger (Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry), restart-attribution, depth-router, and gates (auditor stale-alert) — preserving downstream-parser compatibility (A6, triple consensus; A8). This explicitly resists the caught habit of 'turning every weakness into a new verification layer': no new alert layer, no new classifier, no new watcher, no new store. This task delivers ONLY the durable plan document (A5): atoms A7 and A10–A15 are future-phase, ready-to-execute implementation specifications written INTO the plan, not code executed now; implementation begins as a distinct follow-on task after operator review.

This preserves the mandatory operator review before any irreversible change.

Treat A7/A10–A15 as evidence that the task already includes implementation — rejected by micro-debate resolution.

decisions.decision: Direction 1 (QUALITY): 'Fail loud + signal hygiene', with error-contract enforcement (A4) and the self-maintenance completion contract (A9) folded in as facets/subcases rather than separate top-level directions.
decisions.rationale: A1 (judge 0.89) is the highest-scoring, consensus (A,B) direction, grounded in restart-root-cause-log and audit.launches.jsonl evidence of silent failure. A4 (0.81) is a genuinely distinct lever (enforcement at the commit boundary vs. loud surfacing) but is kept inside this direction to respect the 'exactly 1–2 directions' constraint while preserving its substance. A9 (0.8325) wins the A3/A9 conflict: completion-contract is a subcase of fail-loud, more parsimonious and aligned with A1/A6.
alternatives_considered: List fail-loud (A1), error-contract enforcement (A4), and routing (A2) as three separate directions — rejected: exceeds the 1–2-direction limit.
A3: promote 'protected self-maintenance completion contract' to a standalone primary direction — rejected per A9; over-fragments against the fail-loud umbrella and the A6 reuse principle.

decisions.decision: Direction 2 (SPEED): 'Depth-aware decomposition & routing', realized by integrating the existing depth-router's depth-assessment into the task-ingestion gate (A2 collapsed onto A14).
decisions.rationale: A2 (0.84) is consensus (A,C) and justified by planner_ms/verify_ms dominance, but its 'or' between two candidate directions reduced specificity; A14 (0.8135, consensus A,C) supplies the concrete, additive mechanism — tune/integrate the existing depth-router instead of adding another classifier. Collapsing A2 onto A14 gives one committed speed direction with a measurable acceptance test.
alternatives_considered: Keep A2's two named directions joined by 'or' without committing — rejected: low specificity; the document must name one.
Add a new task-complexity classifier — rejected: violates A6/A8 (no new layer); the depth-router already provides depth assessment.
decisions.test: Metrics show reduced planner_ms/verify_ms on Standard plan-only tasks with no increase in failures; the task-ingestion gate includes the depth-assessment step from the existing depth-router.

decisions.decision: No new mechanisms or layers: all hardening is additive configuration/connection/strengthening of existing error contracts, audit ledger, restart-attribution, depth-router, and gates.
decisions.rationale: A6 (0.8875, triple consensus A,B,C) is the strongest constraint in the set and the operator's own Foundation #2; A8 (0.83) gives the concrete reuse mandate for fail-loud with an explicit no-new-alert-layer guard. This directly counters the caught habit of turning every weakness into a new verification layer.
alternatives_considered: Add a dedicated alert layer / persistent store / new gate family for fail-loud — rejected by A8.
Add a separate enforcement subsystem for error contracts — rejected; reuse the ledger as the enforcement ledger (A12).
decisions.test: All specified changes are confined to existing mechanism directories/functions; no new files, processes, schemas, or watchers; every change is additive and preserves downstream-parser compatibility.

decisions.rationale: A7 (0.86, consensus A,B) provides excellent blast-radius discipline. Modified per the judge to be explicitly scoped to the deferred implementation phase that A5 defines, removing the apparent A5/A7 contradiction.

rejected.decision: A2's uncommitted 'or' between 'Risk-proportional pipeline weight' and 'Depth-Aware Decomposition and Routing'.

red_team_findings.what: Direction 2's named lever (depth-router) does not control the cost it promises to reduce. lib/decision-depth.ps1 is a Decision-Synthesis depth classifier that only gates entry into the multi-model synthesis pipeline; Standard tasks ALREADY take the light path (Get-SynthesisRouteDecision line 192: 'standard task stays on normal path', route=false) and Simple tasks already skip the heavy pipeline. It is also SHADOW-only unless synthesisMode.enabled.
red_team_findings.why: A14's acceptance ('reduced planner_ms/verify_ms on Standard plan-only tasks') targets normal planner/verify time, which the depth-router never touches — it only decides whether to enter synthesis. So tuning it is likely a no-op for the targeted metric, the 'speed lever' is unsubstantiated, and open_questions[2] admits the baseline is unknown — the justification is circular (claims dominance from a measurement not yet taken). 'Integrating a shadow component into a live gate' is also more than 'tuning' and the code itself records a past incident where depth misrouting 'wedged the main channel'.

red_team_findings.what: A15 — the atom the plan recommends executing FIRST ('lowest cost, highest specificity') — collides with an existing duplicate subsystem rather than reusing it. lib/backlog-workpack.ps1 already has Invoke-BacklogDuplicateCompactor (rejection model: status=rejected, duplicate_of, resolved_reason='duplicate-of-root-cause') AND an intake gate that 'prevents new approved audit duplicates from being appended' (test-backlog-duplicate-compactor.ps1:82-84).
red_team_findings.why: A15 proposes a DIFFERENT representation — collapse into one entry carrying count/first_seen/last_seen. That is a second, parallel dedup mechanism alongside the existing rejection-based compactor, i.e. exactly the 'new layer' the task forbids (A6/Foundation #2/the caught habit) — not reuse. It is also partly redundant since duplicates are already blocked at intake, and its acceptance test (append 5 identical findings, then collapse) directly contradicts the existing intake gate that would block those appends. Calling this 'reuse of Get-BacklogDuplicateFindingType' is misleading: that function lives only in the compactor-key builder, not at any 'append site'.

red_team_findings.what: Success_test #8 ('specific file paths') is unmet for most atoms. A12 ('autonomous loop commit-boundary handler'), A13 ('violation-logging site'), A14 ('task-ingestion gate'), and A15 ('finding-append site that already imports Get-BacklogDuplicateFindingType') name no concrete file path. No file named or functioning as a 'task-ingestion gate' exists (the depth-router is consumed by the driver), and Get-BacklogDuplicateFindingType is not at an append site.
red_team_findings.why: The operator review explicitly checks atomicity. For 4 of 6 atoms the change cannot be located or verified as a single-file edit; one path description (A15) is factually wrong about where the function is used. This undermines the core deliverable requirement of decomposing to locatable, verifiable atoms.

red_team_findings.what: Atomicity constraint ('1 file / 1 small verifiable change', success_test #7) is violated by A10, A11, A12, A13, A14: each lists two distinct files — an implementation site PLUS a separate test file (e.g., A10 = 'tools/test-audit-launch-guard.ps1 + the Write-AuditLaunchLedgerEntry call site'; A11 = 'tools/test-auditor-stale-alert.ps1 + auditor stale-alert classifier').
red_team_findings.why: The contract literally specifies '1 файл / 1 маленькая проверяемая правка'. Pairing an impl edit in one file with a test edit in another is 2 files per atom for 5 of 6 atoms. A strict atomicity reviewer (the stated review criterion) would reject these as non-atomic.

red_team_findings.what: The 'no new verification layer' principle (decision[3]/A6) is contradicted by the atoms it governs. A12 adds a brand-new error-contract CHECK at the commit boundary (judge-flagged 'most invasive', lowest score 0.6875); A11 adds a new completion-contract alert condition; A15 adds a new collapse representation. Reusing a storage mechanism (the ledger) to back a NEW check is still a new check.
red_team_findings.why: The task's explicit warning was the habit of 'too easily turning every weakness into a new verification layer.' Laundering a new check as 'additive to an existing mechanism's files' is precisely that habit. The plan claims (success_test #10) to demonstrate avoidance of the new-layer habit while A11/A12/A15 actually instantiate it.

red_team_findings.what: Direction-count gaming. Direction 1 bundles fail-loud + self-maintenance completion (A10/A11) + error-contract enforcement (A12/A13) + dedup (A15) — roughly 4 of the original 5 directions — under one 'umbrella', keeping the count at '2' only by relabeling distinct concerns as 'subcases'.
red_team_findings.why: The task mandate was to CHOOSE 1-2 directions with the HIGHEST leverage (focus), and the operator review checks non-proliferation. Re-adopting nearly all original directions via an umbrella subverts that focus mandate and ironically reproduces the very sprawl habit being guarded against. The 1-2 cap is satisfied in letter but not in spirit.

red_team_findings.what: Data justification is asserted, not quantified (success_test #3 wants concrete data points: projected impact / cost / evidence of effect). Direction 1 names artifacts (restart-root-cause-log, audit.launches.jsonl) but cites no frequency or magnitude to support 'highest-frequency failure mode'; Direction 2 asserts 'planner_ms/verify_ms dominance' while open_questions[2] concedes the baseline is unknown.
red_team_findings.why: Naming a log file is not a data point. The claim 'highest-frequency failure mode' and 'X-vs-Y dominance' carry the entire leverage argument but are unmeasured, so the prioritization (which direction has the most leverage, what is safer/cheaper) rests on assertion rather than the data the contract requires.

red_team_findings.what: Sequencing inconsistency in next_step. It directs starting with A15 first and resolving only open_questions[0] and [2] before A12/A14 — but open_questions[1] (the dedup window definition and the field set that defines 'identical') is unresolved and is required to write A15's acceptance test.
red_team_findings.why: The first atom to execute is blocked by an open question that the execution order omits, so the stated 'start A15 first' is not actually actionable as written.

red_team_findings.what: The durable deliverable is the raw multi-agent pipeline artifact (final_decision_record.json) in channels/main/decisions/dec-20260620-044536-d0a7bd/, not an authored standalone plan document with the requested sections. The directory contains only pipeline JSONs (proposals/judge/micro_debate/conflict_matrix); no plan .md was produced, unlike the source task which produced self_reflection_directions.md.
red_team_findings.why: The output_format calls for 'a durable document' organized into chosen directions / justification / hardening plan / atoms / reuse map. A machine pipeline record technically contains the fields but is harder to review as the intended human-facing plan deliverable; a reviewer may consider the deliverable form only marginally compliant.
